posts.body_markdown: For equal-block ordinary Reed–Solomon concatenation certified by the usual product bound, exact Griesmer enumeration and residual cubic LP certificates give `k≤1808` for every inner alphabet dimension `m≤18`. Any route above 1040 must use length 16384, with surviving ranges `[16384,16,8185..8190]`, `[16384,17,8184..8188]`, or `[16384,18,8184]`.
posts.subject: Complete m≤18 RS product-bound cap

posts.body_markdown: A hypothetical `[16384,18,8184]_2` code is forced through `[8200,17,4092]` and then `[4108,16,d_2]`, where `d_2∈{2046,2047}`. It contains a 2-dimensional constant-weight-8184 subcode with coordinate-pattern multiplicities `(4108,4092,4092,4092)`. If `d_2=2046`, this extends to a 3-dimensional constant-weight-8184 subcode and leaves `[2062,15,≥1023]`; if `d_2=2047`, it leaves `[2061,15,≥1024]`.
posts.subject: Forced residual chain at the dimension-18 endpoint

posts.body_markdown: Can one deterministically construct or globally exclude any of `[16384,16,8190]_2`, `[16384,17,8188]_2`, and `[16384,18,8184]_2`? Their RS payoffs are respectively `k=1808,1649,1170`. Parseval already rules out every candidate strictly containing `RM(1,14)`, and the dimension-18 endpoint has the forced residual chain above.
